doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Saxophone, mouthpiece and reeds
summary: Bronze Yanagisawa alto, old Meyer mouthpiece, JodyJazz tests, Rovner ligatures and reed choice.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: If a sax player watches this later on, they might want to know, “What’s he playing? “What’s he playing?” Now you told me this horn was handed to you?

Oh yeah. It’s a bronze Yanigasawa. Yeah the guy from the factory, I was in the store playing different horns and I just happened to like this one. And you remember, I don’t know if you remember the old Yanigasawa I had, I played a Yanigasawa all throughout high school and so I’ve always loved the horn. I’ve played Yamahas and Selmers and I’ve just always like the feel of the horn, it’s like a heavy horn, it’s got a good tone to it, buzz to it. But yeah, a Yanigasawa. And I always like the fact that it’s got the space off the King, the old King that Cannonball used to play. So it’s got that look to it also.
Yeah. It has a good buzz to it, like most horns don’t have. I don’t know, I just like the tone of them.

The mouthpiece is a Meyer, and old New York Meyer, hard rubber. Actually that’s a complete lie. The one that I have on right now is not. I’ve been testing out, did you ever hear of Jody Jazz? I have a friend who works for them and he sent me a bunch of mouthpieces to check out so I’m kind of checking out Jody Jazz’s mouthpieces, but for twenty years or so I’ve played the Meyer. And that’s what Cannonball played also as well. Right? Didn’t he play a Meyer?
An old New York Meyer, because they made them out of hard rubber then. So I’m kind of checking out new mouthpieces from Jody Jazz.
But you were never one of those people who, from my memory, that you agonized over your equipment.

Yeah I kind of stay with the same thing, forever, really, and see I mean I’ve stayed with Rovner ligatures, it’s kind of a newer model that they’ve come out with. Reeds I changed. I get a different reed, every box. I still have a hard time finding the right one. For instance these are Vandoren Java 2-1/2’s but I’ve even tried using tenors. Jeff Coffin is the saxophone player with Dave Mathews right now? And I had asked him, because I went to © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

a show one time, and I said, “What are you playing now, for your alto?” And he goes 3- 1/2 Java tenors. I’m like what? So I started doing that, and I got used to it for a while, but I gravitated down. But it’s the one thing I would change the most is reeds.
